title: DSMB Enrollment Hold Authorization Chain After SAE Cluster
question: As of April 15, 2026, what is the site's regulatory compliance gap, and what is the immediate required action?

contributor.name: James Osei-Bonsu
contributor.title: Clinical Trial Operations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Protocol amendments, IRB submissions, informed consent versioning, FDA regulatory compliance

choices: No compliance gap exists — the enrollment hold is sponsor-directed and the site appropriately paused screening; IRB notification is only required once the formal DSMB letter is received.

The compliance gap is the unauthorized disclosure of DSMB-confidential information in the unofficial Slack channel; Priya's message implies the hold is safety-related, which could constitute unblinding. Immediate action: report to sponsor and document in deviation log.

The compliance gap is the missed IRB notification deadline — the SOP requires notification within 10 business days of an enrollment hold, the regulatory affairs team advised filing, but no submission exists in SharePoint as of April 15. Immediate action: file IRB-4C form with the DSMB email as supporting documentation.

The compliance gap is that Subject 1887-068 remains in screening status without a documented hold rationale in their study record — the site must formally withdraw the subject from screening or document the hold in Epic.
